question: Which of these lines is parallel to 3x + 2y = 5?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any linear equation **ax + by = c**, all lines parallel to it are of the identical form **ax + by = k** (where k ≠ c).

The given line is 3x + 2y = 5.

By comparing the options, only the equation 3x + 2y = 7 matches this exact a and b coefficient format.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x + 2y = 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The equation of the original line is 3x + 2y = 5.

**Concept Used:**

Two lines are strictly parallel if their slopes are equal (m₁ = m₂).

For a line represented as ax + by = c, the slope m is determined by −a/b.

 3x + 2y = 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Slope of the given line 3x + 2y = 5 is m = −3/2.

⇒ Let us calculate the slopes of all given options to find the identical one:

⇒ 1) 3x + 2y = 7 → Slope = −3/2 (Parallel to given line)

⇒ 2) 2x + 3y = 5 → Slope = −2/3 (Not parallel)

⇒ 3) 3x − 2y = 5 → Slope = 3/2 (Not parallel)

⇒ 4) x + y = 5 → Slope = −1 (Not parallel)

⇒ Only the first equation has the same slope as the original given line.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x + 2y = 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines Condition

Two general lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 are strictly parallel and do not touch when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.

Perpendicular Lines Condition

Two lines cross each other at exactly 90 degrees if the mathematical product of their slopes equals −1 (m₁ × m₂ = −1). The perpendicular inverse format is bx − ay + k = 0.

Intersecting Lines Condition

Linear graphs will always intersect at exactly one unique point if they possess structurally different slopes, proven when a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

Coincident Lines Condition

Two drawn lines represent the exact same path and hold infinite solutions universally if their constants are fully proportional: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
